KEY MESSAGE 1...A developing Nor'easter east of the Mid-
Atlantic coast lifts to the north, then retrogrades back towards
New Jersey over the weekend before finally departing on 
Tuesday. This will bring periods of rain and strong winds at the
coast to the region.

Broad high pressure remains centered over eastern Canada and 
extends back into the Great Lakes. While the high will weaken 
and lift into northern portions of the Province of Quebec, it 
will still be strong enough to create a tight pressure gradient 
between it and low pressure east of the Mid-Atlantic. The trend 
with the last run of models has been to bring the storm closer 
to the shore, and even have the center of the Nor'easter move 
into New Jersey Saturday night. 

A tight north to northeast pressure gradient develops tonight 
and will persist through the weekend as this Nor'easter 
retrogrades back towards New Jersey Saturday through Saturday 
night. Winds increase tonight, generally to 25 to 35 mph with 40
to 50 mph inland, and gusts up to 60 mph at the coast. Will 
keep High Wind Warnings and Wind Advisories in effect through 
Saturday night, but additional headlines may be needed on Sunday
depending on the strength and position of the low on Sunday. 
This trend may result in stronger winds farther west as well. 
Given that trees still have their leaves, the combination of 
these winds and heavy rain (more on that in a bit) will result 
in tree damage, as well as power line and potentially roof 
damage with highest impacts at the coast.

The farther inland trend also results in higher PoPs inland as 
well as and higher rainfall over the area. Rain spreads into the
region from east to west starting late tonight, and then on 
Saturday, PoPs will be 60 to 70 percent across the southern 
Poconos, Lehigh Valley, and far northwest New Jersey and 80 to 
90 percent across the rest of New Jersey, southeast 
Pennsylvania, and Delmarva. PoPs will then be 90 to 100 percent 
across the whole area Saturday night and Sunday. QPF has also 
increased, with 1 to 2 inches of QPF north and west of 
Philadelphia and across Delmarva, and 2 to 4 inches along the 
I-95 corridor, and as much as 3 to 5 inches over much of eastern
New Jersey. This will be over a 48 to 60 hour timeframe, so 
widespread flooding is nor anticipated at this time, though 
there may be some flooding concerns by late Sunday and Sunday 
night. In addition, runoff from this rain may exacerbate coastal
flooding, which will be covered by Coastal Flood Warnings. 
Cannot rule out a few embedded thunderstorms, mainly at the 
coast, during this time.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Multiple rounds of significant tidal flooding 
expected into this weekend. Major Coastal Flood levels are now
expected for the New Jersey Atlantic Coast, the Delaware 
Atlantic Coast, and portions of central and southern Delaware 
Bay. The Coastal Flood Warning has been expanded to northern 
portions of Delaware Bay.

With a slow moving nor'easter and multiple days of strong 
northeast winds expected, the confidence in the threat for tidal
flooding remains high. In fact, the threat for the New Jersey
Atlantic Coast, Delaware Atlantic Coast, and portions of
southern Delaware Bay to reach Major Flood levels around the 
time of high tide Saturday morning has increased, so we have 
increased the forecast for these areas to reach Major Flood 
levels. Strong onshore flow that has persisted for several days
is resulting in water piling up across tidal tributaries and 
within back bays of coastal communities. Tidal levels will also 
be enhanced with astronomical tides increasing with the upcoming
Full Moon Saturday. 

For Delaware Bay communities, north/northeast winds will keep 
pushing water to the west side of the Bay and onto the Delaware 
coast. This will increase the forecast for Major Flood levels 
around southern and central Delaware. The Coastal Flood Warning 
remains 2 AM Sunday for Kent and Sussex, DE. The forecast is now
expected to reach the Moderate Flood level for Cumberland and 
Salem, NJ as well as New Castle, DE, so the Warning was expanded
to these area.

For the tidal Delaware River, widespread minor tidal flooding 
continues to be forecast, so the Coastal Flood Advisory remains
in effect through Saturday Night for the tidal Delaware River. 
While not currently expected, we cannot rule out Moderate tidal
flooding getting to Delaware River communities. 

As mentioned above, more north/northeasterly winds will limit 
the tidal flooding threat for the Chesapeake Bay. Some spotty 
minor tidal flooding is anticipated at Claiborne, but nothing 
higher than that at this time. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Dangerous rip currents and high surf are 
expected at the Jersey Shore and Delaware Beaches through 
Sunday. Beach erosion is likely and breaching of sand dunes is 
possible.
